findings.text: the fragment this commit edits still names psi_write_factor(DD3_CONVENTION) as the pulsedesign writer's mechanism, which is the function this same commit deletes at nova/imas/pulsedesign.py:30, and line 168 instructs the sample.py follow-on to adopt that same deleted helper; the node's own evidence artifact therefore cites a symbol that no longer exists and directs the follow-up work to an ImportError, while the code at nova/imas/pulsedesign.py:528 now calls dd_equilibrium_factor("3.39.0", PSI_LIKE).

the `provenance is None` early return guards a case that cannot occur: I probed imas 2.3.0 directly and every IDS carries ids_properties.provenance at DD 3.39.0 (74 names) and DD 4.1.1 (82 names), and Metadata.put_properties always passes self.ids.ids_properties (nova/imas/metadata.py:196), so the parent revision's resize-then-hasattr sequence already completes every DD4 write and this commit changes no observed behaviour; the dead branch is the only part of the change that the added tests exercise.

the DD4 arms do not fail if this commit's change is reverted: the hasattr(node[0], "sources") guard predates the commit (it is present at 5326ef004), so the eight parametrised arms pass on the parent exactly as they pass at the head, and the negative control reproduces the parent's guard rather than this diff's; only tests/test_metadata.py:57 exercises the new early return, so the round's durability rests on one assertion.

this file and the new tests/test_metadata.py are outside the source run's declared write paths (the manifest's orientation_write_paths and the brief's 'Write only' list both stop at nova/imas/plasma_source.py and the scenario/reader set) and outside the brief's named test files, so the node widened its own fence rather than asking; this review's dispatch names both paths, which makes the expansion visible but does not make it declared.

another evidence fragment of the same plan still documents psi_write_factor as the writer's mechanism at :31 and :46 and as the declared mutation site at :74; deleting the helper makes all three stale, and a reader following that fragment's negative control can no longer apply it. The file is outside this node's write scope, so it needs a plan section rather than a silent omission.

the comment '#: the IDS names the review found sharing the DD4 layout.' cites a review as the source of a code fact; provenance belongs in the commit message and the source should state why those four IDS names are the set (they are the ones whose DD4 node layout was measured), not who reported them.
